title: Equipment routes during competitive gun combat
scope: Controlled host builds of the native and JKWeb sources. The turn-and-walk physics replay and the stock pickup grant fixture are separate experiments. Live-match pickup attribution is outside this receipt.

equipment_revision.description: Matching source snapshots at the end of the equipment change, at the time of the physical equipment replay.

route_policy.scope: Elite guns mode, outside CTF objectives and directed companion modes.
route_policy.medium: Dry final walks require supporting floor and a body path. A direct underwater leg stays inside one submerged sector. Longer routes use the existing movement graph, including its water, lift and jump edges.
route_policy.combat: Ordinary forward and strafe inputs follow the equipment route while weapon aim and fire remain available. Committed traversal keeps its heading when needed. Low heavy-ammunition reserves, a lost gun, and useful health or shield stock affect destination choice. Newly replicated dropped packs use their synchronized bins and a transient contact point.
route_policy.static_graph: Dropped packs never become persistent graph nodes. Each scan preserves the best connected static goal even if all nearby direct probes fail. The four highest-ranked packs and graph approaches retain their probes. One extra rotating candidate can enter each shortlist.
route_policy.companion_orders: Explicit resource and recover orders use their own item-weighted graph plans while facing an opponent or hearing a cue. Pressure keeps its own combat movement rules.

checks: A visible target four units ahead stays under legal pistol fire while the bot takes a perpendicular, multi-edge route to a concussion rifle 4.2 units away. Recent damage, a Force threat and a projectile cue leave that movement intact.

With an E11 owned and one rail charge in stock, a pack created after graph construction supplies a better goal. An existing reachable node approaches the pack and a short checked final leg brings it into reach. Blocking enemy LOS suppresses firing.

Slot reuse, movement beyond the recorded tolerance, depletion, and pending destruction invalidate a previous pack identity. Full heavy reserves permit shield patrol, and a simulated removal of the owned concussion makes a still-useful pack the next destination.

Pack scoring reads at most the actual layout capacity (12 entries on native, 16 on JKWeb). Invalid entries, unsupported equipment, full ammo, empty contents, expired items, and useful paired gun/ammo contents are covered.

Four better-looking but disconnected racks cannot displace a proven graph route to a fifth rack. A fifth useful drop can also get a checked path past four blocked candidates. Resource and recover commands sustain lateral movement to a shield and legal gun input with an opponent in sight. A projectile cue cannot take over recovery movement when the opponent disappears.
The portal runner checks dry and submerged contact points, player-sized clearance, ordinary pickup reach and vision, and absence of graph-node creation.
dispatcher_regressions.weapon_selection_companion_check: The controlled driver also passes the separate elite-weapon cases for retained heavy readiness, close saber opportunity and bolt defense, separating opponents, elevation, underwater limits, reserve ammo and safe splash clearance.

controls_and_physics.method: A stock-sized pack and stationary opponent are staged at supported graph locations. Other pickups are disabled to isolate this decision. Every frame runs jkBot_Tick and ordinary player look and movement controls, followed by stock floor attachment, collision, physics and body rotation. Force is disabled. A fire-input frame counts as moving above 0.1 world units/second. Completion requires ordinary pickup-sphere overlap with physical line of sight. The weapon COG and the item grant are outside this experiment.
controls_and_physics.units: The per-condition results are identical between the two source trees. Each row represents two trials. Opponent departure at 2 seconds is scripted.

stock_grant_fixture.setup: A separate host-compiled JKWeb fixture puts the player at a verified pack contact in synthetic sector geometry. It invokes stock sphere intersection, LOS, the item collision callback and mechanically compiled stock backpack touched/taken handler bodies. A loopback adapter delivers the original client and authority message handlers in process. Media effects are stubbed and stock automatic weapon switching is disabled. The full COG VM and a live network session are outside this fixture.
